title: Bouncing ball

reference.basis: striped bar length is not stated and is not a standard size

slow_motion.evidence: no captions, narration or visual indication of slow motion; motion appears as real-time animation

subjects.description: small shiny blue spherical ball that falls and bounces

observation.what_happens: A small blue ball drops from beneath a black-and-white scale bar at upper left and bounces repeatedly while drifting rightward across the frame. The motion starts when the ball is released and ends when it comes to rest on the brown surface at lower right.

calibration.note: scale from the fall itself: 2094 px/s² over 7 arcs = g of 9.807 m/s²

given: g = 9.807 m/s² (Earth); it set the scale, so treat g as known and fixed
reasoning: x drifts right steadily while y shows tall parabolic arcs shrinking after each hit near -2.16 m, with the third minimum higher near -2.05 m. That suggests gravity flight plus bounce restitution, near-constant vx, and a floor that rises to the right. Candidates go from pure-gravity flat bounce to sloped frictional bounce to sloped bounce with quadratic air drag for Earth air.

critique.finding: The ball falls under gravity and bounces straight up off a flat floor. Each bounce keeps {e} of its falling speed before hitting {y_floor}.
critique.headline: Ball drops, bounces cleanly on flat floor, settles still.
critique.why_it_won: It adds the bounce that the plain flight law lacks, while slope and air drag add nothing to the fit.
